quote: Ebenso ist es wahrscheinlich beim Auftreten mehrerer Parameter!
english: It is probably the same when several parameters occur!
topic: Hilbert discusses the dependence of solutions of differential equations on a parameter λ, noting that they have poles at the special values of λ, and asks general questions about singularities and branching in the parameter and about whether the coefficient A(x) is determined by the singular values.

triage.modern_statement: Context: Hilbert is looking at a linear boundary value problem such as y'' + λA(x)y = 0 with boundary conditions. The solution, or equivalently the Green's function / resolvent, depends on the spectral parameter λ. It is meromorphic in λ, with poles exactly at the eigenvalues. His remark seems to guess that the same holds when the equation contains several parameters λ1,...,λk: the solutions should depend analytically (meromorphically) on all the parameters together, with singular sets given by the eigenvalue conditions. In modern terms this means (a) solutions of ODEs depend analytically on several parameters, and (b) the multiparameter eigenvalue problem, where the 'eigenvalues' are k-tuples (λ1,...,λk). The same page also asks whether A(x) is determined by the singular values. That is a separate question, the inverse spectral problem, and is not the remark being checked here.
triage.answered_by: There is no single resolution, and Hilbert's sentence is too vague to tie to one theorem. (a) Analytic dependence on several parameters goes back to Poincaré's analyticity theorem, which was already known when Hilbert wrote the note. (b) Multiparameter eigenvalue problems for Sturm–Liouville-type equations were later developed systematically, above all by F. V. Atkinson. He introduced an abstract algebraic framework in the 1960s and wrote the monograph 'Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems' (Academic Press, 1972). This was continued by Atkinson & Mingarelli, 'Multiparameter Eigenvalue Problems: Sturm–Liouville Theory'. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem.

evidence.claim: Poincaré showed that solutions of differential equations are frequently analytic functions of the initial conditions and of any parameters that occur. This supports the analytic-dependence part for several parameters.
Poincaré's theorem: solutions are analytic in the initial conditions and the parameters, provided the right-hand sides are analytic.

Atkinson introduced an abstract algebraic setting for multiparameter eigenvalue problems in the 1960s. He showed that a nonsingular multiparameter eigenvalue problem is equivalent to an associated system of generalized eigenvalue problems.
Atkinson's foundational monograph 'Multiparameter eigenvalue problems' (Academic Press, New York, 1972) is cited as the basic reference for the field.
Multiparameter Sturm–Liouville theory has been set out in book form (Atkinson & Mingarelli) and continues to inspire researchers.

triage.why: The remark is a one-line aside, so I can only read it as 'the meromorphic/pole structure in λ carries over to several parameters'. On that reading, the analytic-dependence part follows from Poincaré-type theorems. The spectral side became multiparameter spectral theory (Atkinson 1972 and later), which is still active, for example in work on singular two-parameter eigenvalue problems. None of the sources I found refers to Hilbert's note, and my search was cut off by the tool limit before I could check the several-variable meromorphic (Fredholm) side. So I cannot confirm exactly which statement Hilbert meant or that a specific later paper resolved it. Confidence is therefore low.
